title: Complaint of TE David Kniseley, et al. vs. Rocky Mountain Presbytery
disposition_detail: SJC answered Issue 1 No and Issue 2 No, meaning Rocky Mountain Presbytery did not err, and denied the complaint. The complainant obtained no issue-level relief; the presbytery's denial of the underlying complaint remained in effect. A concurring opinion and a dissenting opinion were filed.
first_summary: The SJC denied a complaint challenging Rocky Mountain Presbytery's decision allowing a mission church to give an unordained female staff member the title 'Minister of Church Life.' The SJC held that the BCO uses 'minister' as synonymous with pastor and teaching elder, but that the BCO is silent on general use of the title for non-ordained staff, leaving the lower court discretion. Four commissioners dissented.
summary: On complaint from TE David Kniseley and others, the SJC reviewed Rocky Mountain Presbytery's refusal to forbid a mission church from giving an unordained female staff member the title 'Minister of Church Life.' The SJC denied the complaint. It held the BCO uses 'minister' synonymously with pastor and teaching elder, but is silent on general use for non-ordained staff; a lower court may exercise discretion subject to BCO 40-2(3)'s WESP review. The decision addressed only the constitutional issue, not the title's wisdom or propriety; four commissioners dissented.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Lines 1–5, 11–13 identify SJC case 2007-13, 37th GA (2009), Complaint of TE David Kniseley, et al. v. Rocky Mountain Presbytery. Lines 50–53, 107, 109 show the judgment and reasoning were written by the full Standing Judicial Commission; lines 111–121 record the vote (15 concur, 4 dissent, 1 disqualified, 1 abstain, 2 absent).
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 17–38 summarize the overture and complaint: RMP adopted a substitute acknowledging 'minister' as synonymous with pastor/teaching elder but allowing generic use for unordained staff; on Sept. 27, 2007, RMP denied Kniseley's complaint without rationale. Lines 38–48 state the complaint to General Assembly and the two issues.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 50–53 answer both issues No; line 107 denies the complaint. The adopted reasoning at lines 57–105 holds that the BCO uses 'minister' for pastor/teaching elder, but is silent on general use for non-ordained staff, leaving lower-court discretion subject to BCO 40-2(3)'s WESP standard. Lines 97–105 limit the decision to the constitutional issue.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Lines 97–105 state the decision does not address the wisdom or propriety of using 'minister' generally and is limited to the record and PCA Constitution. Lines 109 and 111–121 confirm full-SJC authorship and vote. Lines 123–142 and 144–305 are separate concurring and dissenting opinions, not adopted reasons.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Lines 59–75 quote and ratify the JBC advice on Constitutional Inquiry #1 from 1989, including its assistant-pastor interpretation; no separate incorporated judgment with a missing result is presented. The dissent critiques that advice at lines 196–271.
